Count the stuffed animals on the bed. Ask how many there would be if one more snuggled in.
At tuck-in, ask what number comes after five. Then whisper what comes after ten.
During story time, guess how many animals are on the page. Count them together to check!
Give three goodnight kisses, then ask how many would make four. Deliver the extra kiss!
Snuggle up and count backward from ten to one. Land softly on zero and say goodnight.
Offer {name} a choice, four hugs or six hugs. Ask which is more, then pay up!
Tell a tiny tale of five sleepy ducks where one waddles off. Ask how many still snore.
Spot the swings and count them, then the slides. Ask which number is bigger.
Ask {name} to collect eight leaves. Count them, then hunt for one more to make nine.
Take five giant steps toward the slide, counting loudly. Then try six tiny ones!
Push the swing and count past ten together. See what big number you two can reach!
Gather a handful of pebbles at the park. Guess how many, then count them into your palm.
On the walk home, count the dogs you see. Ask if you spotted more dogs or more birds.
While you cook, ask {name} to bring three potatoes, one at a time. Count them as they land!
Crack two eggs, then ask what one more would make. Let the answer sizzle!
Stir the pot ten times, counting together. Then let {name} pick the next number of stirs.
Before counting strawberries into the bowl, ask for a guess. See how close it lands!
Pour scoops of rice and count each one out loud. Stop and ask what number comes next.
Line up five spoons while dinner cooks. Ask how many stay out if two go in the drawer.
Ask {name} to set one fork at each seat. Count forks, then people, and check the match.
Set the table with one plate missing on purpose. Ask how many more plates you need.
Let {name} deal out napkins like cards, counting each one. Ask if every seat got exactly one.
Wonder aloud how many cups the table needs tonight. Add a pretend guest and ask again!
Put out three spoons, then ask for enough for five people. Count how many more arrive.
Scoop the pet's food together, counting each scoop. Ask how many scoops there would be with one extra.
Wonder together how many paws the pet has. Then wonder about two pets!
Pile the pet's treats in your hand and count them. Give one away and ask how many remain.
Point to today's number on the calendar. Ask what number comes right after it.
Peek at the calendar and count the days until the weekend. Clap once for each day!
Spill a few coins on the table. Guess how many, then count them into a cup.
Stack coins into two small piles. Ask which pile has more and how to find out.
